segments.script: In 1184, dozens of nobles died in a pool of human poop. They’d shown up for a political meeting.
segments.spoken_text: In eleven eighty-four, dozens of nobles died in a pool of human poop. They’d shown up for a political meeting.

segments.script: Erfurt, in what’s now Germany. King Henry VI—the future Holy Roman Emperor—has gathered nobles to settle a dispute between an archbishop and a powerful lord.
segments.spoken_text: Erfurt, in what’s now Germany. King Henry the Sixth, the future Holy Roman Emperor, has gathered nobles to settle a dispute between an archbishop and a powerful lord.

segments.script: The room is packed. Beneath them: wooden floors. Beneath those: a latrine pit. You can probably see the structural problem.
segments.spoken_text: The room is packed. Beneath them: wooden floors. Beneath those: a latrine pit. You can probably see the structural problem.

segments.script: The floor gives way. People crash through into the waste below. Dozens die, with the toll often put at around sixty.
segments.spoken_text: The floor gives way. People crash through into the waste below. Dozens die, with the toll often put at around sixty.

segments.script: Henry survives. According to accounts, he’s sitting in a stone window recess that stays intact. Rescuers reach him with a ladder.
segments.spoken_text: Henry survives. According to accounts, he’s sitting in a stone window recess that stays intact. Rescuers reach him with a ladder.

segments.script: He later becomes emperor. But on this particular day, the most valuable seat in the empire was a windowsill.
